acceptanceCriteria: a decision or TCB-V0 amendment states how a merged-forward lane satisfies the cem-verdict gate at the commit complete --commit pins (merge-aware candidate rule or an explicit quiescent-main requirement)
one real native completion through the cem-verdict gate is recorded with its receipt audit (V1-1283 criterion 4) under the chosen rule
touchPaths without trailing slashes are either normalized to prefix keys for the predicate or refused with a named reason
body: Observed 2026-10-13 from the V1-1283 continuation (PR beamfall/corvint#863, head 0de6d5ab8). TCB-V0-015 substitutes {attempt.candidateCommit} with the gate worktree HEAD, and the verdict gate (internal/taskman/cem_verdict_gate.go) refuses sealed-tree-mismatch unless the candidate's tree differs from the sealed map's target (the bind commit) only by the sidecar rename. Native completion (`complete --commit <merge sha>`) requires the submitted tree to be the merge commit tree. When main moved between the lane BASE and the merge, or when a post-seal commit exists, the merge tree differs from the seal tree, so the gate refuses on exactly the commit completion needs. Every lane closed out today (V1-1303, V1-1340, V1-1345) had a moved main. Criterion 4 of V1-1283 (one real completion through the gate) therefore needs either a lane whose merge commit tree equals its seal tree (PR head = seal commit and no intervening merges) or a gate rule that accepts a merge of the seal commit into base whose non-sidecar delta against base is exactly the seal commit's delta. Expected: decide and specify which (TCB-V0 amendment), with the refusal name kept for a genuinely altered tree. Actual: no gate-compatible completion path for the ordinary merge-forward lane. Also: V1-1283's own touchPaths lack trailing slashes so they govern no hunk under touched-anchored (see the lane report); the predicate vocabulary may need a prefix rule.
title: cem-verdict gate: candidate must be the seal commit, but native completion pins the merge commit, so the gate can only grant on a quiescent main
